    <descript>
      <abstract>This report references harvest data of fish species (Clupea pallasi) from Kodiak Island and Cook Inlet and harvest data of invertebrate species (Siliqua patula) from Cook Inlet, Alaska.

  The aforementioned data are referenced in citation: Alaska Department of Fish and Game.  1977.  A fish and wildlife resource inventory of the Cook Inlet and Kodiak areas. Volume 2.  Alaska Coastal Management Program, Division of Policy Development and Planning, 443 p.

  This literature was collected as part of a metadatabase that represents one or more nearshore resources (from physical attributes such as water and air, to birds and mammals).  Each entry is viewable in three formats, 1) a geospatial explicit format (ArcView 3.3) named GIS ArcView 3.3 Near GEM project, 2) a spreadsheet format (Excel 2002 and within ArcView) named GEM Nearshore Metadata Set, and 3) a ProCite database named GEM Nearshore Metadata References, which consists of references included in 1 and 2 above.  The ProCite database record number corresponds to the Excel Procite Number.  Reference Procite #22 for this literature's metadata.

  The metadata are maintained in digital format (ArcView 3.3, Excel 2002, and Procite) and are available from the Alaska Science Center, USGS in Anchorage, Alaska.

  For a detailed description of the three databases and the project, see "Bodkin, J. L., and T. Dean.  2003.  Alternative Sampling Designs for Nearshore Monitoring (Gulf Ecosystem Monitoring and Research Project G-030687), US Geological Survey, Alaska Science Center, Anchorage, Alaska." available on-line at http://www.evostc.state.ak.us/pdf/GEM_final_reports/030687.pdf.</abstract>
      <purpose>Part of the design effort of the "Alternative Sampling Designs for Nearshore Monitoring" (Gulf Ecosystem Monitoring and Research Project).  Provides a comprehensive historical perspective of locations and types of past studies conducted in the nearshore marine communities within Gulf of Alaska in the form of a geographical information system database.</purpose>

<metadata>
  <idinfo>
    <citation>
      <citeinfo>
        <origin>Dr. Wieslaw Maslowski, Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, California, USA</origin>
        <pubdate>Unknown</pubdate>
        <title>Results from the Naval Postgraduate School Arctic Modeling Effort</title>
      </citeinfo>
    </citation>
    <descript>
      <abstract>The Naval Postgraduate School 18-km coupled Arctic Ocean and sea ice model
employs the Parallel Ocean Program (POP) adapted to the Pan-Arctic region and coupled to a parallel version of the Hibler dynamic-thermodynamic sea ice model with viscous-plastic rheology and a zero-layer thermodynamics approximation. The model grid is configured on a rotated spherical coordinate system and its resolution is 1/6° (~18 km) with 30 levels. The model domain extends from Bering Strait through the Central Arctic, Nordic and Barents Seas into the sub-polar North Atlantic (to ~45°N) and it includes the Canadian Archipelago. Daily-averaged operational atmospheric fields from the European Centre for Medium-range Weather (ECMWF) for 1994-98 are used to force the model in addition to the 1979-93 reanalyzed data. It is important to note that the only interannual forcing in the model comes from the prescribed atmospheric fields. The model has been integrated initially for 200 years forced with 1990-94 atmospheric fields. It was then spun up for 20 years using the repeated 1979 annual cycle, which was followed by an additional 2-decade integration using 1979-1998 atmospheric data.
The new 9-km coupled ice-ocean model, developed at the Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) in Monterey, California, USA, is configured on a 1/12° and 45-level rotated spherical grid.  It consists of a regional adaptation of the POP, developed at the Los Alamos National Laboratory, coupled to a parallel version of the original Hibler dynamic-thermodynamic model with a viscous-plastic rheology.  The model uses ECMWF daily-averaged reanalyzed data for 1979-1993 and 1994-2002 operational products, including the surface incoming long wave and shortwave radiation, 2-m air temperature and dew point temperature, and 10-m winds.  The model incorporates a 2.5-km bathymetry field, developed by the International Bathymetry Charting of the Arctic Ocean project, interpolated to the 9-km grid.  The model domain extends from the
Pacific Ocean (~30°N) through the Central Arctic, Nordic and Barents Seas into the North Atlantic (to ~40°N) and it allows realistic exchanges through Bering Strait.  Results from the ongoing model integration are just becoming available.</abstract>
      <purpose>To advance the knowledge of Arctic Ocean dynamics and variability.  The model
provides large scale and long term data, while maintaining high resolution for better analysis.</purpose>
    </descript>

rows.source_object: NPS18km/30level and9km/45level Arctic ice/ocean model results and detailed model setup.
rows.actual_XML_content: The XML contains substantive description of algorithms, grid resolutions, vertical levels, geographic domain, forcing products/periods, spin-up history and bathymetric input. It has no code/configuration file, forcing arrays, grid coordinates or model-output field. Its -180/180/90/30 coverage box is consistent with a pan-Arctic model domain, but broad bounds are not a confidentiality determination.
rows.material_gap: Two primary papers support much of the described scientific architecture, but differ in domain/forcing endpoints and do not expressly delimit the source permission/DOD-sensitive clause. They do not prove every configuration statement in the exact2003 XML was released, nor that sensitive model outputs are now unrestricted.
exact_source_quotes: Permission of Contributor required. Department of Defense Sensitive data
Results from the ongoing model integration are just becoming available.
rows.research_outcome: Primary NPS-author papers were read at publisher/author-institution URLs. The2000 paper substantially corroborates the18km setup/spinup; the2004 paper corroborates the9km setup. The old official NPS department page links to a NAME page that now returns404. The2003 Polar Research paper independently links the18km and9km model comparison, but is not blanket release authority.
rows.next_agent_action: Seek the original public2002–2003 NAME model-description page or a release-scoped contemporaneous report, compare every unmatched source clause, and preserve source restrictions. Public scientific similarity is useful evidence, not declassification. An independent reviewer may assess whether source-positive results/object context plus existing separate restoration authority suffices, but this packet does not recommend clearing909 now.
